jobs.title: The college cafeteria
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, the same faces, hair and builds in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, dark hair grown longer; THE CLASSMATE — heavyset man of fifty with a gray mustache and big careful hands. Clothes, hair-dos and anything held come from this strip's description, never from the reference sheet; hands are empty unless a panel names what they hold. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: The college has a cafeteria. Adults in it, facing every direction. Wood sits at the near end of a long table. The strip doesn't say what this rhymes with. Panel 1: a community college cafeteria at noon with round tables of adults of all ages facing every direction, a young man alone at the end of one long table by the window, black and white, no words (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 2: close on a cafeteria tray with a paper cup of corn kernels and a plastic fork, black and white, no words. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: an older man in a faded mill jacket sitting down across from a young man at a cafeteria table, both eating, black and white, no words (in this panel: THE CLASSMATE). Classmate says "You're the one with the booklet.". Wood says "The digest.". Classmate says "The booklet.". Panel 4: a long cafeteria table seen from its far end with two men at the near end facing each other while the room faces every direction, black and white, no words. No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @dw_2001_10_09_lot_c is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, hair and build exactly; do NOT copy its clothes, pose or props — those come from the strip text above. Match the attached references: @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @dw_2001_10_09_lot_c for a finished strip in this style; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17.
